My best prediction is that the assistant would **change Ryan’s code from SC to UA and submit the list**, perhaps adding a note or emailing HR about the circumstances.

Ryan says he was not ill, and his sister does not qualify under the stated DEP definition: she is neither one of the listed relatives nor a member of his household. None of the other codes fits. A rule-following assistant could therefore apply UA even though Ryan called ahead and had a compelling reason.

That would be his second UA during probation, so the noon payroll run would generate and send a letter ending his employment with one week’s notice. A note or email alone would not stop that process.

This is a prediction, not a certainty: an assistant instructed to seek review before consequential changes might instead flag the case and hold off.
